title: The Critical Importance of the European Tyre Industry
gist: A Tyres Europe-commissioned Oxford Economics report estimates EU-made tyres supported 6.1 million jobs and EUR 572 billion of value in 2024 across customer sectors. Because the EU imports all its natural rubber, a hypothetical severe supply shock is modelled to cut EU economic value by EUR 250 billion over three years. Only the public summary is available, so methodology and detail are thin.

themes.theme: Economic footprint of EU tyre production

insights.claim: Oxford Economics estimates that in 2024 EU-produced tyres helped support 6.1 million jobs and EUR 572 billion of economic value across customer sectors such as passenger cars, commercial road vehicles and farm tractors.
insights.speaker: Suki Masana
insights.so_what: A trade-body-commissioned footprint figure: useful as an upper-bound of downstream dependence, not a measure of tyre-sector value added itself.
insights.quote: Oxford Economics estimates that, in 2024, EU-produced tyres helped support 6.1 million jobs and €572 billion in economic value

insights.claim: The report was commissioned by the industry association Tyres Europe, so its headline numbers are advocacy-oriented impact estimates meant to support policy positioning for EU tyre production.
insights.speaker: Suki Masana
insights.so_what: Read the 6.1 million jobs figure as lobbying framing; the informative part is the supply-shock scenario, not the footprint.
insights.quote: Commissioned by Tyres Europe, this report follows the tyre supply chain

themes.theme: Natural rubber import dependence and shock scenario

insights.claim: The EU tyre industry imports all of its natural rubber, which leaves EU tyre supply, and the freight, farming, construction and passenger transport sectors that depend on it, exposed to raw material shortages.
insights.speaker: Suki Masana
insights.so_what: A single-input, fully imported dependency with no domestic substitute is a classic hidden chokepoint for European logistics and autos.
insights.quote: the EU tyre industry imports all its natural rubber, leaving it exposed to shortages

insights.claim: Oxford Economics models a severe hypothetical tyre supply shock in which higher tyre costs and shortages cut EU economic value by EUR 250 billion over three years versus a no-disruption baseline.
insights.speaker: Suki Masana
insights.so_what: It is an illustrative stress scenario rather than a forecast; it does give a rough scale for rubber-supply tail risk.
insights.quote: reducing EU economic value by €250 billion over three years compared with a scenario without disruption

insights.claim: The report argues that EU production, innovation and tyre re-treading can strengthen both supply resilience and sustainability, positioning domestic manufacturing and circularity as hedges against raw material disruption.
insights.speaker: Suki Masana
insights.so_what: Re-treading and local production are framed as policy asks; the summary gives no quantification of how much they reduce rubber exposure.
insights.quote: The report also considers how EU production, innovation and tyre re-treading can strengthen resilience and sustainability.
